Post-retrofit utility data were collected in the years following implementation to evaluate performance under comparable climatic conditions. Energy use intensity (EUI) was reported in terms of annual kBtu/ft² (thousand British thermal units per square foot1) for each full calendar year of available data. EUI is defined as the total annual energy consumption normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building, providing a standardized metric for comparing energy consumption across years; the higher the EUI, the less efficient the building. The initial EUI (83.1 kBtu/ft²) was calculated using the Tribal Office utility bills from the pre-retrofit period. These data form the basis for evaluating the effectiveness of the retrofits over time. Energy use intensity per heating degree day (EUI/HDD) was reported in terms of annual kBtu/ft2 for the available calendar years for the building. EUI/HDD is the annual energy usage first normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building and normalized again by the base 65°F HDD for the observed year. HDDs are the cumulative difference in daily mean temperature from a baseline temperature. More heating degree days occur in colder locations and generally correlate to higher energy usage. EUI/HDD was calculated using actual heating degree data from the Bethel Airport weather station (60°46’47.0″ N, 161°50’16.0″ W; elevation 125 ft), obtained via the Alaska Climate Research Center’s Data Portal, which provides an interactive interface to the United States Department of Commerce, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s weather records. Bethel was used as the reference station because Aniak is too small to have its own weather station or historical climate data. Energy cost index (ECI) was reported in terms of annual dollars per square foot for the available calendar years. ECI is the annual utility costs for electricity and fuel oil normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building. ECI costs are all expressed in 2024-dollar values and do not include Power Cost Equalization (PCE), a State of Alaska administered economic assistance program that provides utility cost relief to rural utility customers.2 Typically, EUI and ECI follow similar patterns, but the ECI 1 kBtu/ft² (thousand British thermal units per square foot): A measure of building energy use, showing how much energy is consumed per square foot of floor area. 2 The Power Cost Equalization (PCE) program is a state initiative of the State of Alaska that helps reduce the cost of electricity in rural communities, where rates are often several times higher than in urban areas. Many of these communities are small, isolated, and rely on expensive diesel fuel (different from #1 Fuel Oil) for power generation. PCE is funded through investment earnings from the PCE Endowment Fund, which is managed by the Alaska Permanent Fund Corporation.
